title: Introduce ephemeral endpoint auth + per-AZ NAT failover and rollback hooks
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: private control planes occasionally experience single-AZ egress failures that cause long-lived endpoint authorizations and tear-down difficulties during upgrades. This PR introduces two coordinated sets of changes: 1) ephemeral IAM-authorized VPC endpoint tokens that expire/refresh as part of the control-plane lifecycle, reducing long-lived peering surface and simplifying cross-account cleanup; 2) per-AZ NAT failover mapping with deterministic priorities and a small rollback hook framework to ensure safe upgrades and fast recovery when an AZ loses egress.

What this does (summary):
- Adds a new terraform module (terraform/modules/ephemeral-endpoint-auth) that provisions a short-lived KMS-wrapped token and an accompanying Lambda-style rotation function for PrivateLink endpoints. The module exposes variables for rotation window and cross-account role ARNs.
- Extends the existing vpc-egress module with per-az priority lists and an optional lightweight health-probe lambda that updates route tables to prefer healthy NATs. The default behaviour is non-destructive: routes are updated only when both health-probe and config agree.
- Introduces an installer-side rollback hooks framework (installer/hooks/rollback.md + scripts) so that upgrades which change endpoint auth or nat mappings can register a revert action. Hooks run as part of canary -> full rollout and are idempotent.
- Adds Helm chart bump for private-installer-controller (charts/private-installer/Chart.yaml) and a reconciliation controller change that watches the ephemeral token secret and forces a controlled rebind when rotation is detected.

Checklist: [x] terraform module with tests, [x] installer hooks documented, [x] Helm bump + controller change, [x] e2e in perf-canary stack, [x] roll-forward and rollback tested in staging.

Compatibility & migration notes:
- By default the ephemeral auth module is opt-in. Existing stacks will not be affected unless the new module is enabled.
- Enabling per-AZ NAT failover requires a brief reconciliation window that may rewrite a small set of route table entries; the rollback hook will reinstate previous priorities if any unexpected failures are observed.
- KMS cross-account key policies are required when endpoints are shared across accounts; examples included in module README.

Related: ENG-9724 (ephemeral endpoint lifecycle), ENG-9801 (per-AZ egress reliability), SUP-3172 (customer reported long-lived endpoint leak).

review_comments: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Can you add an explicit IAM policy example for the cross-account rotation role? Also prefer using context-based logging in the lambda so we can index it in Datadog.
Asha Patel (author): Added full policy example to the module README and switched the lambda to structured JSON logs. PTAL.
Lina Berg (reviewer): The route table updates need an exponential backoff; a transient API throttling in some accounts caused a reconciler loop during canary. Please add guard and max retries.
Asha Patel (author): Implemented backoff and added a safety window to prevent flips within 30s. Updated tests to exercise transient failures.
Samir Kapoor (approver): Verified terratest in staging and observed zero packet loss during a simulated AZ egress outage. Approving to merge.
release_notes: Add opt-in ephemeral endpoint auth and per-AZ NAT failover with rollback hooks. New terraform module: ephemeral-endpoint-auth. Helm chart bump for private-installer controller. Backwards compatible and opt-in by default.
